summary: Three distribution lists for sending out Network documents such as RFCs. One is for sites sending their own documents to liaisons, and the others are for the Network Information Center to reach other participants and station agents. These were postal lists with names and addresses, not email lists. It was replaced by RFC 300.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 211 gives three postal mailing lists and says who should receive each kind of network document. It replaced RFC 168 and was later replaced by RFC 300.

subtitle: Three mailing lists for distributing RFCs and other network documents

tldr.problem: Sites and network participants needed an organized way to receive RFCs and other documents by mail.
tldr.mechanism: Sites use List A to send their own documents to liaisons; the NIC uses Lists B and C for other participants and station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 211 replaced RFC 168 and was later replaced by RFC 300.

facts.label: Station-agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week or more often when quantity warrants

sections.title: Using the Three Lists
sections.content:
Sites use List A when distributing their own documents, to get RFCs to liaisons quickly. All mail other than local mail should be sent by air mail.

The NIC uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site network participants and station agents. The document also notes that a separate distribution list for the Network Graphics Group had been sent to that group.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC assigns a different list to each distribution job. Sites send their documents to liaisons through List A, while the NIC uses Lists B and C for other recipients.

sections.title: Liaisons and Network Participants
sections.content:
List A is the initial distribution list. It includes network liaisons and others who should receive RFCs whether the document comes from the NIC or a site. These contacts also receive selected catalogs and other formal documents from the NIC.

List B is for network participants who receive formal NIC documents, either when a mailing goes to liaisons or when documents are sent to station agents. The RFC lists names and postal addresses for the recipients.
sections.plainLanguage: List A covers the initial recipients of RFCs. List B covers other network participants who receive formal documents from the NIC.

sections.title: Station Agents and Replacement
sections.content:
List C names NIC station agents. They receive copies of documents distributed to liaisons and documents sent as part of a station collection. The NIC says it mails to station agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.

RFC 211 says it obsoletes RFC 168. The unit metadata records RFC 300 as the RFC that later obsoleted RFC 211.
sections.plainLanguage: List C identifies station agents who receive copies for their sites. RFC 211 replaced an earlier list and was later replaced by RFC 300.
